title: It was the second product from a team whose first was a video game that flopped.
description:
It was the second product from a team whose first was a video game that flopped. That game was Fates Forever, a mobile MOBA released in 2014.

Sold his previous company, mobile gaming platform OpenFeint, to Japan's GREE for $104 million in cash, then used the fresh start to found Hammer & Chisel and build a game.

While building it, the team kept hitting the same wall: voice and text chat for gamers hadn't meaningfully improved in a decade. TeamSpeak and Skype were still what most players were stuck with.

Discord launched publicly in May 2015, aimed straight at the problem Fates Forever had run into. Same team, same instinct, a completely different product.

Discord's user count by the end of 2017, up from 3 million less than two years earlier, gaining roughly 1.5 million new users a week.
